metadata.remarks:
Secure Network is a composite pattern expressing the institutional position that network connectivity is acceptably safe for use. This assertion is valid only when connectivity is intentionally established, segmented into trust zones, admission-controlled, policy-mediated, continuously monitored, and responsive to detected misuse.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern serves as the enterprise network trust statement. It introduces no new controls or technical mechanisms. A system may claim to operate on a secure network only if all referenced constituent network patterns are realized and assessed.

components.title: Network Core
components.description: Foundational network connectivity, addressability, routing, and baseline trust boundaries.

components.title: Network Segmentation and Zones
components.description: Separation of network trust domains to limit exposure and lateral movement.

components.title: Network Access Control
components.description: Admission control to the network based on identity, posture, and context.

components.title: Network Mediation and Policy Enforcement
components.description: Inspection and enforcement of permitted network communications.

components.title: Network Remote Access
components.description: Controlled extension of network connectivity beyond institutional boundaries.

components.title: Network Wireless Access
components.description: Secure use of broadcast and proximity-based network access.

components.title: Network Third-Party Connectivity
components.description: Managed and bounded network access for external entities.

components.title: Network Monitoring and Response
components.description: Visibility, detection, containment, and response at the network layer.
